exposure: type of ectopic pregnancy (right-sided ampullary tubal)
cohort: The study included 31 patients diagnosed with ectopic pregnancy and admitted to a tertiary medical institution between January 2023 and January 2024.
finding: The study found an incidence of 4.2 ectopic pregnancies per 1000 deliveries, with a substantial proportion of cases presenting in a ruptured state (67.7%) requiring salpingectomy (64.5%), and identified previous cesarean section and sterilization as notable risk factors.
mod_finding: A history of cesarean section was identified as a notable risk factor for ectopic pregnancy, with the study suggesting a potential rise in ectopic pregnancy incidence correlating with increased cesarean section rates.
